customer.business: StoreLab (A/B testing for physical retail: simulate store layout and display changes on your own store's data before moving a shelf)
customer.target: Owners and operations/merchandising heads of mid-size Philippine convenience and mini-mart chains (20 to 500 stores) that already run CCTV in their stores; all prices are in Philippine pesos (PHP)

segments.name: Owner-operator of a 20-60 store regional chain
Head of operations or merchandising at a 60-200 store chain
Commercial or category director at a 200-500 store chain

behaviours.name: Gut-feel merchandiser
behaviours.how: Decides layouts from experience and store walks; trusts what has worked before.

behaviours.name: Cost cutter
behaviours.how: Every new monthly fee must show payback within the year; compares against hiring one more staff member.

behaviours.name: Supplier-led displays
behaviours.how: Most endcaps and displays are proposed and paid for by brands; the chain mainly approves placement.

behaviours.name: Data-curious tester
behaviours.how: Already reads POS reports weekly and has tried small store trials; wants better evidence.

behaviours.name: Burned by a tech vendor
behaviours.how: Paid for a system before that nobody used after three months; very cautious with new software.

behaviours.name: Follows the market leader
behaviours.how: Watches what 7-Eleven and Alfamart do and copies what seems to work.

behaviours.name: Needs head-office approval
behaviours.how: Can recommend a purchase but the owner or board signs anything recurring.

objections: A simulation is not real shoppers; why would I trust it?
Our CCTV is old and low resolution; will it even work?
PHP 8,000 a store every month adds up across the whole chain
We have no time or staff to run pilots and move fixtures
Suppliers decide most of our displays anyway
Is this allowed under the Data Privacy Act, filming customers for analytics?
A new company with no customer results yet
What is the payback, in pesos?
habits: you review weekly POS sales by category every Monday
you visit stores on weekends and rearrange displays yourself
you meet supplier sales reps every week about promos and displays
you are under pressure to cut costs after a slow quarter
you watch what the big chains change in their stores
your IT person also handles the CCTV and the POS

pitch:
StoreLab: test store layout and display changes on a simulation of your own store before you move a shelf.
It uses the CCTV and POS data you already have. No new sensors. Shoppers are tracked anonymously, with no faces and no identity.
You type a goal (for example "+10% snack sales, don't slow the checkout"). StoreLab proposes changes, tests each one on simulated shoppers built from your store's data, and gives you a pilot plan with test and control stores.
Price: PHP 8,000 per store per month on a 12-month contract, minimum 10 stores. Setup is included.
StoreLab is a new company with no customer results yet.
